summary.intent: Continue a stacked-PR release workflow: fix the title of PR 253, then create and ship PR 4, which makes the product announcement wait for the asset owner's tag in the release derivation graph.
summary.outcome: PR 4 branch was created with a derive.rs change, a new plugin tag prerequisite test, an updated pinned snapshot, updated spec and docs, and a changeset. CI was run, and the commit was pushed with the stack extended and its title and body set.

repo: Release derivation lives in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs and uses OpIndex plus artifact/forge derivation logic.
Release behavior is documented in both docs/architecture/release.md and docs/specs/release.json, and both must be updated when derivation changes.
Derive output is covered by a pinned snapshot that must be updated and diff-reviewed when graph prerequisites change.
The repo uses changesets, so each PR needs a changeset file.
Work is organized as a stack of PRs (PR 4 is branched on the previous ones), and the stack's title and body must be updated when extending it.
Tests use a helper for forge publish lookup, which was read before writing the plugin tag prerequisite test.

code.finding: The product announcement operation now has a prerequisite on the asset owner's tag, so announcements wait for the tag. This was done near add_artifact_uploads and was covered by a new plugin tag prerequisite test.

workflow: Review the snapshot diff after updating pinned snapshots to confirm only the intended graph edges changed.
Run the full CI check locally before committing and pushing a stacked PR.
Read existing tests and helpers before adding new ones so they follow the same conventions.

friction: The title of PR 253 was wrong and needed fixing before continuing, and the other PRs in the stack had to be checked for similar problems.
open_items: The other PRs in the stack were checked, but the transcript does not show what was found, so their titles and bodies may still need a follow-up.
The transcript does not show whether CI passed, only that it was run.
